clue.text: Went fast cycling behind flash bikes

parts.note: a flash is a moment, abbreviated MO

indicators.note: cycling means the first letter of the word is moved round to the end

parts.note: went fast means sped, past tense of speed

explanation.surface: Someone races off on a bike behind a showy set of motorcycles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' looks like riding a bike but says the first letter of the speeding word moves to its end; MO for 'moment' is a standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Small motor-assisted two-wheelers with pedals are motorised bikes of a low-powered kind.

clue.text: One's hard on end of man's lead?

definitions.text: One's hard on end of man's lead?

indicators.note: on end of says the following pieces are attached after the first one
the lead of a word is its first letter, so take the start of man's

parts.note: one gives A, the apostrophe-s read as is
hard means stiff, rigid

explanation.surface: A big dog straining hard at the end of its owner's leash.
explanation.walkthrough: M (lead of 'man's') then A STIFF ('one's hard') placed 'on end of' it. The whole clue also describes a large dog pulling on a leash.
explanation.definitionFit: This breed is a huge, powerful guard dog, the kind that pulls hard when walked on a leash by its owner.

clue.text: Concealed diamonds when entering country

indicators.note: entering means the card suit goes inside the country's name

parts.note: Peru is a South American country
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: Smuggled gems slipped into a country out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: A French borrowing used in English for hidden or lost from view, as a soldier lying in wait.

clue.text: Liverpool supporter's chilled about crucial match

indicators.note: about means the combined letters are turned round

parts.note: Liverpool FC are the Reds, so a supporter is a Red
chilled means iced

explanation.surface: A Liverpool fan is cold before the big game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses REDICED to give the answer. Liverpool football club play in red and are nicknamed the Reds.
explanation.definitionFit: A deciding game settles a tied contest, so it is the crucial one.

clue.text: Darn idiot in school

indicators.note: in places the fool inside the school abbreviation

parts.note: a tit is British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: An exasperated 'Darn!' at a fool in class.
explanation.definitionFit: To darn is to mend with needle and thread, sewing a small repair.

clue.text: Books? Lad essentially after a model car

indicators.note: after puts the books and the lad's centre behind the model

parts.note: a model, as of a train or plane, is a toy
OT is the Old Testament, books of the Bible

indicators.note: essentially means the central letter of the word lad

explanation.surface: A boy reading after building a model car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a model' looks like a car model; here a toy is a model in miniature, and 'after' places the books and the boy's centre behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese manufacturer whose name stands for a motor vehicle it makes.

clue.text: Turning against it, one might go around end of can?

definitions.text: Turning against it, one might go around end of can?

parts.words: Turning against it, one might go around end of can?
parts.note: a kitchen gadget is turned against the lid of a tin and travels round its rim

explanation.surface: Someone opposed to an idea circles a lavatory, or a gadget circles a lid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning against it' sounds like opposing something; literally the gadget is turned while pressed against the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen tool cuts round the top of a metal food container by being cranked.

clue.text: No goals? Premier League, primarily has entertaining, fair games

indicators.note: entertaining means holding inside, as a host holds guests

parts.note: taken as written
a nil-nil score is written 0-0, read as two Os

indicators.note: primarily means the first letters of Premier and League

explanation.surface: A goalless football match is still entertaining, fair play.
explanation.walkthrough: A nil-nil draw is written 0-0, read as two letter Os; 'fair' is a funfair, not fairness.
explanation.definitionFit: Ring-tossing contests are classic stalls at a funfair, where prizes are won.

clue.text: Stormy Daniels: "Trump and I being cautious with this"

indicators.note: stormy means turbulent, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The adult-film actress Stormy Daniels comments on her discretion about Donald Trump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stormy' is her real stage first name but here signals rearranging DANIELS, TRUMP and I.
explanation.definitionFit: The doctrine or practice of prudence, putting careful self-interest first, amounts to acting with caution.

clue.text: Addict stealing heroin from escort

indicators.note: stealing means the drug is taken away from the escort

parts.note: an usher escorts people to their seats
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A drug addict pinches heroin from an escort.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug consumer is a regular taker, so slang for one dependent on drugs.

clue.text: Holding, touching and keeping it up

parts.note: holding means carrying, as a bag
touching means on, resting against

explanation.surface: Two lovers hold and caress each other and keep going.
explanation.definitionFit: Persisting or continuing an activity is a colloquial phrase meaning not stopping.

clue.text: Sloppy smacker on cheek, mostly

indicators.note: on means the money comes after what precedes it
mostly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: lip is impudence, cheek
a smacker is British slang for a pound, a quid

explanation.surface: A wet kiss planted on someone's cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smacker' looks like a kiss but is slang for a pound coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Runny or watery like a fluid, so sloppy in texture.

clue.text: Go out to pee in the morning over large tree

parts.note: to go out with someone is to date them
pee is how the letter P is said, and P is also slang for urine

indicators.note: over means the morning letters arch over the size letter

parts.note: AM means in the morning
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Instructions to go outside and relieve oneself against a big tree at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' puts AM around L, giving ALM.
explanation.definitionFit: A palm species bearing sweet brown fruit is a tropical plant of desert oases.

clue.text: Child is bad then well

parts.note: food gone bad has gone off
a spring is a well, a source of water

explanation.surface: A child goes from sick to healthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well' looks like healthy but is a water source.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's progeny or descendants include any son or daughter.

clue.text: One in field with summer wear and t-shirt?

parts.note: shorts are worn in summer
a t-shirt is a top

explanation.surface: A sportsperson out on the pitch in summer kit.
explanation.walkthrough: In baseball the fielder stationed between second and third base has this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A baseball fielding position between second and third bases, so a player in the field.

clue.text: Responsibility towards me

parts.note: on can mean towards, as in marching on the city
us is colloquial for me, as in 'give us a kiss'

explanation.surface: Someone feels a duty owed to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Us' for 'me' is northern British usage, as in 'give us a hand'.
explanation.definitionFit: A burden or duty placed on someone, as the burden of proof.

clue.text: Position to make out

definitions.meaning: a place or location, as a nice place by the river
to make out is to see or notice

explanation.surface: A spot where couples go to kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make out' also means to kiss, a surface trap.
explanation.definitionFit: A location is a place, and to see something faintly is to pick it out.

clue.text: Deposits blocked by current accounts

indicators.note: blocked by means the deposits have the current stuck inside them

parts.note: stores are deposits, stocks put away
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Bank deposits stuck in current accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current accounts' looks like a bank phrase but is split: current gives I, accounts is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Narratives or tales told of events are accounts given.

clue.text: Rubbish or good liar? Leader comes out with his crap

indicators.note: the leader comes out means the first letter of the liar is removed

parts.note: a liar is a fibber

indicators.note: crap means poor, so the letters of his are badly arranged

explanation.surface: Is that nonsense, or is he a good liar? The boss comes out with his rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader comes out' drops the F of FIBBER, leaving IBBER; 'crap' rearranges HIS into ISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaningless talk or nonsense is spoken drivel, rubbish.

clue.text: Tend to gorge, briefly cutting portion

indicators.note: cutting means the shortened gorge cuts into the portion

parts.note: a bit is a portion

indicators.note: briefly means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: an abyss is a deep gorge

explanation.surface: A tendency to overeat, cut down by eating small portions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gorge' looks like a verb meaning overeat but is a ravine; 'briefly' drops its last letter before it goes 'cutting' into the portion.
explanation.definitionFit: To look after children while parents are out is to tend to them.

clue.text: Cleaner put on dirt?

parts.note: put on means feigned, a sham
poo is excrement, filth

explanation.surface: Is a cleaning product just smearing dirt about?
explanation.definitionFit: A hair-washing liquid is a cleansing product.

clue.text: What's in milk crate at home?

parts.note: a crate is a case
in means at home

explanation.surface: A crate of milk bottles left on the doorstep at home.
explanation.definitionFit: The main protein found in dairy products such as cheese is a component of milk.

clue.text: Customers pay, go down

parts.note: to foot the bill is to pay it
to go down is to fall

explanation.surface: Shoppers pay up and prices drop.
explanation.definitionFit: Retailers' term for the number of people entering a shop, its visitor count.

clue.text: In pub he might pull bachelor with designer cut

indicators.note: cut means the last letter of the designer's name is removed

parts.note: Giorgio Armani is an Italian fashion designer

explanation.surface: A single man in designer clothes might pick someone up in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pull' looks like picking up a date but means drawing beer from a tap.
explanation.definitionFit: A bartender draws pints by pulling the handle of a beer pump.

clue.text: Have sex with man

definitions.meaning: British slang verb for having intercourse with someone
a male first name, as borne by the actor Moore or the tennis player Federer

explanation.surface: A blunt proposition about a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude British slang for copulating, and also a common boy's name.

clue.text: Lovers in film with clothes discarded at the start

parts.note: a film is a thin layer, as a mist on glass

indicators.note: discarded at the start means the first letter of the clothes is thrown away

parts.note: dresses are clothes

explanation.surface: Lovers in a film shed their clothes in the opening scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' looks like a movie but is a thin haze.
explanation.definitionFit: Women having affairs with married men are their kept lovers.

clue.text: He's one pinching parking spaces

indicators.note: pinching means holding the parking letter tight inside

parts.note: He is the chemical symbol for helium, which is one example of a gas
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A man nicks parking spaces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' looks like a man but is helium.
explanation.definitionFit: Openings or empty intervals between things are spaces.

clue.text: Prosecute to restrict member that's lying

indicators.note: to restrict means to hold in, so the limb sits inside

parts.note: to sue is to take legal action
a pin is slang for a leg, a limb

explanation.surface: Taking a lying member to court to rein them in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lying' looks like telling untruths but means lying flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying on one's back, face upwards, is the posture meant.

clue.text: One might play record way before radio's finale

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
ere is a poetic word for before

indicators.note: finale means the last letter of radio

explanation.surface: A DJ plays a record before the end of a radio show.
explanation.definitionFit: A hi-fi sound system plays vinyl discs and other recordings.
